text: The Samajwadi Janata Party (Rashtriya) (SJP(R)) was established on 5 November 1990 by Chandra Shekhar, who later served as prime minister of India from 1990 to 1991. He led the party until his death on 8 July 2007, at which time he was the party's only member in the Lok Sabha. The party was formed when Shekhar and Devi Lal split from the governing Janata Dal. The SJP(R) secured 60 MPs and formed a government with the support of the Indian National Congress (Indira), with Shekhar as prime minister, which lasted from 10 November 1990 to 21 June 1991—seven months in total—before collapsing when the Indian National Congress (Indira) withdrew its support. S. R. Bommai served as president of the Karnataka state unit of the party until the state unit merged with the Janata Dal prior to the 1994 Karnataka Assembly elections. As of 2012, Kamal Morarka, a former cabinet minister in Chandra Shekhar's union government, was the head of the party, and its headquarters were located at Narendra Niketan, ITO Indraprastha Estate, New Delhi, India.
